messages:
maya: quick heads-up — canary ci for short-seq traffic shows a regression on L4/T4/A10 compared to last week, ~+8-12% p95 latency for 8-32 token requests. attaching quick numbers below.

samir: repro? which model and bench flags?

maya: repro command i used:
```
./bench/serve --model=llama2-13b --device=L4 --batch-size=8 --tokens=16 --profile=perf.json
```
results (median of 5 runs):
```
device  avg_ms  p95_ms
A100    48     63
H100    45     60
L4      72     80  <-- regressed from 66/72 last week
T4      75     82
A10     68     76
```

jonas: bench-bot can you paste the hot-kernel summary from the profile? :eyes:

bench-bot: hot kernels (top 6 by self-time):
```
1) gemm_fused_block32  34.2%  (high l2/warp divergence on L4)
2) kv_read_prefetch    20.5%  (sync memcpy spikes on small batches)
3) softmax_block       12.0%
4) kv_write_commit     9.8%
5) attention_merge     8.7%
6) packing_unpack      4.9%
```

rachel: does KV cache hit-rate look different? maybe small batches cause more eviction/host copies on L4?

maya: yes — KV stats show prefix hit drop from 98% -> 91% with our current merging heuristic when sequences vary a bit in the batch. seems like extra `kv_prefetch` calls are happening.

samir: digging in — our kernel-pick heuristic is currently sequence-length driven only, with a global breakpoint at 64 tokens that chooses fused-block kernels. that made sense for A100/H100 where big fused kernels win, but on L4/T4/A10 those kernels have poor occupancy and worse bank conflicts for short seqs. we need arch-aware breakpoints.

jonas: agreed. proposal: make autotune pick consider (device.family, seq_len, batch_shape) and add a small-kernel path for devices in {L4,T4,A10} when seq_len <= 64. also tweak KV prefetch threshold so we don't prefetch on microbatches < 4 tokens. short config sketch:
```json
"kernel_presets": {
  "default": {"breakpoint_seq": 64},
  "arch_overrides": {
    "L4": {"breakpoint_seq": 32, "use_small_gemm": true},
    "T4": {"breakpoint_seq": 32, "use_small_gemm": true},
    "A10": {"breakpoint_seq": 48}
  },
  "kv": {"prefetch_threshold": 64, "prefetch_batch_min": 2}
}
```

rachel: can we measure impact quickly? even a 5% latency drop on L4 would be great. Also we should gate changes behind canary for Dedicated customers.

maya: ran a quick local patch to force small-gemm on L4 for seq<=32, results:
```
L4 old: p95 80ms -> L4 patched: p95 70ms (12.5% improvement)
T4 old: p95 82ms -> patched: 74ms (9.8% improvement)
A100 unaffected (diff <1%)
```

samir: nice. looks like kernel choice was the main regression. two follow-ups: 1) KV cache merging logic creates extra prefetches when variable seqs are coalesced — reduce cross-seq coalescing for small-seq workloads. 2) add device-level autotune sweep to confirm chosen breakpoint across models and batch sizes.

jonas: for the autotune sweep i can run matrix across {L4,T4,A10,A100,H100} x seqs {8,16,32,64,128} x batch {1,4,8}. expecting small-gemm wins on low mem/low-sm devices for seq<=32. i'll queue jobs on the farm.

rachel: timeline? if results hold we should hotfix runtime config and ship to canary tomorrow, then promote to prod rollout in 48h if no regressions. also prepare rollback (flip to global_breakpoint).

maya: i'll open a small PR with the config override + unit test for kernel selector and include perf numbers. drafting description now.

samir: also log an action item to update docs for "device-aware breakpoints" so support knows why behavior differs by GPU.

jonas: one more note from flamegraphs — L4 shows a lot of time in `kv_read_prefetch` memcpy; small-gemm path reduced memcpy contention because it avoids extra compute-to-copy switching. add a metric for host->device memcpy rate in the tracing.

rachel: ok sounds good. canary patch + autotune results to #eng-runtime tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all, will tag you in the PR: @samir @jonas

samir: :clap:

bench-bot: scheduled autotune jobs: job-9871, job-9872, job-9873. will post results when finished.
